title: Co-option of lysosomal machinery shapes the evolution of the intracellular photosymbiosis supporting coral reefs.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the authors' GitHub repo (FragPipe outputs, figure inputs). Downloaded and parsed Symbiosome_enriched_proteins.csv (179 rows x 33 cols, all 'SymEnriched'), Control_enriched_proteins.csv (1,212 rows) and the full stats table vignette_run_Aipnorm_stats.tsv (2,032 detected proteins; only 621 have a p-value/log2 fold change, 1,411 are missing in too many replicates). Six control and six symbiosome replicates; Known_symbiosome_genes.csv lists ~20 known markers (RAB7A, V-ATPase subunits, NPC2). No protein sequences in the repo. PRIDE keyword search for 'Aiptasia symbiosome' returned nothing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was available (Cell, paywalled, no PMCID). The paper's protein counts, the mass-spectrometry raw-data accession and licence were not seen; the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2025.10.09.679812) was found but not read.

a1_downloadable.note: Processed tables download freely from the authors' GitHub repo (checked); raw-data deposit not located.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Columns 'Enrichment' and Control.Symbiosome_log2FoldChange/AdjPVal give symbiosome-enriched vs control-enriched per protein (checked in files).

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequences are not in the repo, but AIPGENE IDs map to one Aiptasia proteome FASTA file (single download, not thousands of lookups); not yet downloaded.

a4_units_stated.note: Log2 fold change and CycLoess-normalised log2 intensities, named in column headers (checked).

a5_enough_rows.note: 179 symbiosome-enriched plus 1,212 control-enriched proteins = 1,391 labelled rows for classification (checked); only 179 positives, so marginal.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <5 MB of tables plus a ~15 MB proteome FASTA
a6_fits_laptop.note: Tiny; ESM-2 embeddings of ~2,000 proteins run on CPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Repo files are internally consistent (stats table 2,032 detected); paper's counts not seen because full text is paywalled, so unconfirmed.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is measured mass-spec enrichment of purified symbiosomes vs control fraction, not a model output; independent of sequence features.

B1.why: Two label files plus a stats table joined on AIPGENE ID; sequences need a separate proteome FASTA.

B2.why: CSV/TSV files parsed first try with pandas (checked).

B3.why: One experiment, one normalisation (CycLoess) by the authors.

B4.why: Many proteins missing in replicates (1,411 of 2,032 lack statistics); 'detected only in one fraction' needs a policy.

B5.why: One row per AIPGENE protein ID in the files checked.

B6.why: Column names are readable but no data dictionary; paper methods not read.

C1.why: Asking whether general localisation predictors recover a cnidarian organelle is informative either way, but small.

C2.why: DeepLoc 2.0 predicts lysosome localisation generally; nothing for symbiosomes specifically was found.

C3.why: Diversity angle: a non-model animal organelle absent from localisation training sets; weak overall.

C4.why: Symbiosome purification plus mass spectrometry is lab-intensive and done for very few species.

C5.why: DeepLoc 2.0 lysosome score as an off-the-shelf baseline; no published number on this set.

D1.why: ESM-2 open weights for protein sequences.

D2.why: ~2,000 embeddings cached once on CPU, logistic-regression head.

D3.why: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; repo licence not checked.

E1.why: Sequence-identity cluster split is possible on the protein sequences.

E2.why: 1,391 proteins give many clusters, though only 179 positives.

E3.why: Majority class and DeepLoc lysosome probability are obvious dummies.

E4.why: Six replicates per fraction let enrichment noise be estimated (checked in columns).

E5.why: Known markers (V-ATPase subunits, RAB7A, NPC2) in Known_symbiosome_genes.csv must score high.

E6.why: Label shuffle and sequence-length-only ablation are trivially runnable.

E7.why: Only an older small symbiosome membrane proteome (Peng 2010) found; no year or species column.

E8.why: No published ML number exists on this dataset.

G1.why: AIPGENE IDs plus Swiss-Prot best-hit accessions; UniProt mapping via BLAST hits, not direct.

G2.why: UniProt/Human Protein Atlas lysosomal annotations via homology; plausible but loose.

G3.why: Best-hit homology mapping is many-to-one (paralogs, e.g. two NPC2 genes).

G4.why: Could ask whether symbiosome membership is predictable from lysosomal sorting signals; modest question.

H1.why: One lab, one species, one symbiont strain; negatives are present (control-enriched).

H2.why: Missing-replicate proteins systematically low-abundance; membrane proteins under-detected in mass spec.

H3.why: Claim limited to one anemone experiment with 179 positives.

H4.why: Contaminating algal proteins removed by authors (Bmin-removed folder), but residual co-purification unknown.

I1.why: Coral symbiosis labs (Cleves lab) might prioritise candidate genes for CRISPR from predictions.

I2.why: Could rank candidates in coral proteomes lacking symbiosome proteomics.

I3.why: No clear decision-maker beyond a handful of labs.

I4.why: Cross-species transfer to coral would be the use, but unvalidatable without coral data.

J1.why: Small tables, CPU-only, a weekend project.

J2.why: Need to fetch Aiptasia proteome FASTA and match AIPGENE IDs.

J4.why: Outside typical ML venues; niche audience.

J5.why: Main risk: 179 positives too few for a stable head beyond DeepLoc.

existing_models.name: DeepLoc 2.0 (ProtT5-based multi-label subcellular localisation predictor, 2022)
existing_models.score_and_split: Evaluated on homology-partitioned curated eukaryotic/human sets with a Lysosome/Vacuole class; specific numbers not retrieved.

integration.partner_dataset: UniProt / Human Protein Atlas lysosomal localisation annotations via Swiss-Prot best hits
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Is membership of a newly evolved symbiotic organelle predictable from ordinary lysosomal targeting signals?

controls.positive_control: Known symbiosome markers (V-ATPase subunits, RAB7A, NPC1/NPC2) listed in Known_symbiosome_genes.csv should rank at the top.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffle; sequence-length-only and abundance-only models.
controls.external_validation: None strong; Peng et al. 2010 Aiptasia symbiosome membrane proteome is a small, older possible check.

honest_claim_h3: In one Aiptasia symbiosome proteome, a sequence model can (or cannot) separate 179 symbiosome-enriched proteins from 1,212 control-enriched ones better than a general lysosome-localisation predictor.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's amino-acid sequence to predict whether it sits in the coral-anemone organelle that houses symbiotic algae.
plain_idea.train_on: Sequences of 1,391 sea anemone proteins measured in purified symbiosome vs control fractions (verified counts: 179 enriched, 1,212 control-enriched).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the protein is enriched in the symbiosome, from mass-spectrometry comparison of six purified symbiosome samples against six controls.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Tells coral biologists whether existing lysosome predictors already flag symbiosome proteins, so they can pick CRISPR candidates in corals without doing organelle proteomics.

more_or_better_data.why: Ours covers a cnidarian organelle absent from DeepLoc 2.0's curated eukaryotic training data, but only 179 positives.

confidence_score.why: Six replicates per fraction give per-protein noise estimates; DeepLoc gives probabilities but not calibrated for this organelle.

models_beatable.why: DeepLoc 2.0 (2022, ProtT5, homology-partitioned) is strong generally but was never trained on symbiosomes.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No additional joinable dataset measures symbiosome enrichment the same way; the task differs from DeepLoc's labels.

label_elsewhere.sources: Lysosome localisation in UniProt and Human Protein Atlas (known resources) as a proxy; symbiosome proteomes only from Peng et al. 2010 (found in search).
label_elsewhere.join_key: Swiss-Prot accession via BLAST best hit
label_elsewhere.why: Proxy lysosomal labels allow pretraining, but the exact symbiosome label exists essentially only here.

ambitious.why: Would need a clear result that symbiosome membership is predictable and transfers to coral proteomes.

realistic.why: A small benchmark of localisation predictors on a non-model organelle fits a short methods note.

fallback.why: A negative result (DeepLoc fails on symbiosomes) is still a citable note for the coral symbiosis community.

pitch.headline: A rare purified-organelle proteome from a sea anemone: 179 symbiosome-enriched versus 1,212 control-enriched proteins, six replicates each side.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Organelle-level proteomics of a symbiotic compartment in a cnidarian, with measured negatives; such data exist for almost no other species.
pitch.the_win: An ESM-2 head beating DeepLoc 2.0's lysosome probability in PR-AUC (precision-recall area under the curve) on sequence-clustered held-out proteins.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We learn whether general lysosome predictors already capture symbiosome membership, which tells coral labs if they can skip new proteomics.
pitch.who_wants_it: Cleves lab and other cnidarian symbiosis groups choosing CRISPR knockdown candidates in reef-building corals.

ml_idea: Embed Aiptasia proteins with ESM-2, train a logistic head for symbiosome enrichment with sequence-cluster CV, compare against DeepLoc 2.0 lysosome scores, then score a coral proteome for candidates.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: ~2,000 proteins at a few per second with ESM-2 150M on CPU.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Download the Aiptasia proteome FASTA and confirm all 1,391 AIPGENE IDs map to sequences; then check DeepLoc 2.0 lysosome AUC on the 179 positives — if already >0.9, drop it.

verdict_reason: Clean, open, measured labels, but only 179 positives from one experiment in one species, no external validation, and a narrow audience; a weekend benchmark at most.
